Chapter 5: Love as Discipline and Delight.
When it comes to marriage, love is one of those words that gets tossed around a lot, but let’s be honest—it's often misunderstood. Most people think love is just a feeling, something that drifts in and out depending on what’s happening in life. But real love? It’s so much more than that. It’s both a discipline and a delight.
That means love isn’t just something you fall into—it’s something you choose, something you practice, and something you nurture, day after day.
In the beginning, love feels almost effortless. There’s energy, passion, and excitement—everything seems possible. But as the years move on, those feelings might start to fade a bit, replaced by the routines and responsibilities that come with everyday life.
And it’s right there, in those ordinary moments, that love really shows what it’s made of. Because love becomes a discipline—a daily choice to be kind, to be patient, to show generosity, even on the tough days when it doesn’t come naturally.
I remember hearing about a couple who’d been married for decades. Someone asked them the secret to their lasting relationship. You know what they said? It wasn’t grand gestures or over-the-top declarations. It was the little things—a cup of coffee shared in the morning, a gentle touch, a few encouraging words.
Those simple acts, done over and over, built a sturdy foundation of trust and affection.
Now, love as discipline doesn’t mean you have to hide your feelings or pretend everything’s always perfect. Not at all. It’s about making the choice to act with love, even when your emotions aren’t exactly lining up. It’s about being committed to someone’s well-being, choosing—sometimes quite intentionally—to put their needs ahead of your own.
But let’s not forget, love is also a delight. There are those wonderful moments of joy and laughter—a deep connection that makes all the effort feel worthwhile. These are the times when the beauty of the relationship really shines through. They’re like little gifts, reminding you of all the goodness and grace marriage can bring.
Most of us dream about a love that’s both passionate and lasting. But here’s the secret: passion and endurance aren’t opposites. In fact, they go hand in hand. The discipline of love sets the stage for delight, and those delightful moments give you the strength to keep choosing love, even when it gets hard.
So, marriage becomes this incredible journey—a chance to keep learning how to love, in new and deeper ways. It’s about discovering joy in the everyday moments, and truly celebrating the miracle of two lives, side by side.
